beats.narration: A model answers questions about a picture. I want the real path from pixels to answer — and whether it even needs the picture.
beats.narration_text: Visual question answering with transformers: show me the exact path from pixels and words to an answer, tell me how much accuracy survives if I hide the image, and give me one test I can run on any VQA model.

props.command: Visual question answering with transformers: (1) show me the exact path from pixels and words to an answer, (2) tell me how much accuracy survives if I hide the image, and (3) give me one test I can run on any VQA model.

beats.narration: I'm Ritik. Give a model an image and a question, it returns an answer. I'll show you the four moves a transformer makes — and the experiment proving most answers never needed the image.

props.title: Visual Question Answering, Blind?
thesis: A transformer answers questions about pictures
in four moves. The fourth is the only reason

roadmap.label: The mechanism
roadmap.body: patches, subwords, attention, an answer head — moves 1 to 3

roadmap.label: The audit
roadmap.body: hide the image and re-score. Move 4, and the whole rubric

roadmap.label: The receipt
roadmap.body: published numbers, on screen, with the paper that reports them

show.event: eyebrow + serif title set, presenter line under it
thesis types in line by line as the sentence lands
three numbered roadmap cards rise in order on 'four moves'

beats.narration: Four moves. Tokenize both inputs into one currency. Fuse them with attention. Pool, then decide. Then audit — because the first three can be flawless and still answer from memory. Move four is the rubric.
beats.narration_text: Four moves. Tokenize both inputs into one currency. Fuse them with attention. Pool, then decide. Then audit — because the first three can be flawless and still answer from memory. Move four is the rubric.

props.heading: The four moves

moves.label: TOKENIZE
moves.detail: image → patches; question → subwords. Both become vectors of the same width.

moves.label: FUSE
moves.detail: attention lets every text token query every image patch.

moves.label: DECIDE
moves.detail: pool the fused sequence, score it, pick an answer.

moves.label: AUDIT
moves.detail: hide the image and re-score. Whatever survives was never vision.

props.keepNote: Keep move 4. Moves 1–3 can be perfect and still be answering from a language prior.

show.event: moves 1-3 slide in from the left, one per spoken move, numbers in grey pills
move 4 arrives with the terracotta pill — the beat's one accent
terracotta rule draws left-to-right under the four, then the rubric line

beats.narration: Move one. Transformers only eat sequences. So the image is sliced into sixteen-pixel patches — a hundred ninety-six vectors. The question splits into subwords at the same width. Pixels and words become the same kind of thing.
beats.narration_text: Move one. Transformers only eat sequences. So the image is sliced into sixteen-pixel patches — a hundred ninety-six vectors. The question splits into subwords at the same width. Pixels and words become the same kind of thing.

props.imageCaption: 224 × 224 px  ·  16 × 16 patches  ·  14 × 14 = 196 patch tokens, each linearly projected
props.question: What color is the umbrella?
props.textCaption: subword tokens, embedded to the SAME width as a patch vector
props.mergedLabel: one sequence  ·  [CLS] + text tokens + [SEP] + 196 patch tokens
props.source: Dosovitskiy et al., ViT, ICLR 2021 (patch tokens) · Kim et al., ViLT, ICML 2021 · Tan & Bansal, LXMERT, EMNLP 2019.

show.event: patch grid draws across the scene on 'sliced into patches'
patch vectors lift out into a strip; the umbrella patch is the terracotta one
the question breaks into subword chips; 'color' takes the accent
both strips merge into ONE bar, ink cells then ghost cells, filling left to right

beats.narration: Move two — the worked example. The token for color becomes a query. It scores every patch; softmax sharpens those scores onto the umbrella. Concatenate into one stack, that's ViLT. Keep two towers and cross-attend, that's LXMERT.

props.heading: Move 2 — fuse by attention
props.readout: a weighted read of the image, conditioned on the question
props.honesty: Illustrative attention field — the shape of the read, not measured weights.
props.source: Dosovitskiy et al., ViT, ICLR 2021 (patch tokens) · Kim et al., ViLT, ICML 2021 · Tan & Bansal, LXMERT, EMNLP 2019.

show.event: QUERY label + the terracotta 'color' chip
raw scores wash over all 196 cells — diffuse, unnormalised
softmax sharpens the field onto the umbrella cells as the word 'softmax' lands
the read-out line; then the two fusion families arrive as named rows

beats.narration: Move three. Pool to one vector, score it with a linear head, pick from a fixed answer list. Most VQA is classification, not generation.
beats.narration_text: Move three. Pool to one vector, score it with a linear head, pick from a fixed answer list. Most VQA is classification, not generation.

props.heading: Move 3 — pool, then decide
props.vocabNote: softmax over a FIXED answer vocabulary — the most frequent training answers
props.honesty: Illustrative distribution — the mechanism, not a measured model output.

show.event: the sequence bar collapses to a single pooled column on 'pool'
the W·h head lights terracotta on 'linear head'
answer bars grow to their probabilities; 'red' takes the accent
the fixed-vocabulary line lands on 'classification, not generation'

beats.narration: Move four. In the original VQA paper, a model that never sees the image lands within nine points of the model that does. On yes-or-no questions, the blind one clears seventy-eight percent. The picture was worth almost nothing.
beats.narration_text: Move four. In the original VQA paper, a model that never sees the image lands within nine points of the model that does. On yes-or-no questions, the blind one clears seventy-eight percent. The picture was worth almost nothing.

props.heading: Move 4 — the blind test
props.bracketLabel: +8.99 points — everything the image was worth
props.callout: On yes/no questions the blind model scores 78.20%.
props.source: Antol et al., “VQA: Visual Question Answering,” ICCV 2015 — Table 2, open-ended task, real images.

show.event: bars grow in order, each number counting up to its published value
the BLIND bar takes the terracotta on 'never sees the image'
bracket draws between blind and sighted; +8.99 label on 'nine points'
the 78.20% yes/no callout lands on 'seventy-eight percent'

beats.narration: The fix is a test you can steal. For every question, find a second image where the honest answer flips. Balanced that way, the language-only baseline drops five points, and the best model of the day drops six.

props.heading: The fix — complementary pairs
props.question: Is the umbrella red?
props.procedure: Workers pick, from 24 nearest neighbours, an image where the answer is different. Not possible for 22% of questions.
props.honesty: Scenes redrawn (illustrative) — the procedure, not the paper’s photographs.
props.source: Goyal et al., “Making the V in VQA Matter,” CVPR 2017 — unbalanced VQA v1 vs balanced VQA v2.

show.event: IMAGE A with the red umbrella and its answer chip, 'yes'
IMAGE B rises beside it — same scene, ink umbrella — answer flips to 'no'
the shared question sits above both; the pair is held side-by-side to the end of the beat
the paired-accuracy rows drop in, each with its −delta in terracotta

beats.narration: The verdict. The four moves are real. The architecture is honest. The benchmark was not. Show me a blind score and a paired score, or I don't know what your model sees.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. The four moves are real. The architecture is honest. The benchmark was not. Show me a blind score and a paired score, or I don't know what your model sees.

artifactLines: The four moves are real: patches and subwords, attention, a pooled answer head.
The architecture is honest — the ORIGINAL benchmark was not: blind scored 48.76 of a possible 57.75.
Balancing is the fix, not a patch: complementary pairs cost every model tested 5–7 points.
No blind score and no paired score means no verdict on what a VQA model can see.
props.sourceNote: Antol et al., ICCV 2015, Table 2 · Goyal et al., CVPR 2017 (VQA v2).

beats.narration: Your turn. Paste this. Take any VQA model and report four numbers: with the image, with the image replaced by noise, on ten pairs you build yourself, and where the attention lands. If the noise number is close, you have a language model wearing a camera.
beats.narration_text: Take a VQA model I can run locally. Report four numbers: accuracy with the image, accuracy with the image replaced by Gaussian noise, accuracy on ten complementary pairs I build by hand, and the fraction of cross-attention mass landing inside the region my question names. Then tell me which of the four moves is actually doing the work.

props.command: Take a VQA model I can run locally. Report four numbers: (1) accuracy on 100 questions with the image, (2) accuracy with the image replaced by Gaussian noise, (3) accuracy on 10 complementary pairs I build by hand — same question, second image, opposite answer, (4) the fraction of cross-attention mass landing inside the region my question names. Then tell me which of the four moves is actually doing the work.
output: GOOD   noise collapses · both pairs right
BAD    noise ≈ real → a language model
SCORE  1 of 2 pairs right = the prior
